B1.title: Sent from the deal's own account
B1.message: The co-signer only signs transactions that move money out of this deal's single-use account, never anything that touches someone else's account.

B2.title: Allowed kinds of transaction
B2.message: Each step may only use the transaction types it needs (payments, closing the account…). Handing control of the account to a new key is never allowed.

B3.title: Network fee is reasonable
B3.message: The XRPL fee must stay under a cap, so a transaction can't quietly drain the account's XRP reserve.

B4.title: Expires quickly if not used
B4.message: A live transaction must expire within a few ledgers (seconds), so a signed one can't be held back and used later. Pre-signed defaults are exempt; they're guarded by the other checks.

B5.title: All-or-nothing
B5.message: When several payments go together, either all of them happen or none do. No half-paid outcome is possible.

B6.title: Pays only people in the deal
B6.message: Money may only go to the guest, the hotel, the arbiters, or the service's fee account, never to an outsider.

B7.title: Closes the account cleanly
B7.message: Closing the account must pay out every last cent and then delete it. If the payouts don't add up to exactly what's in the account, it would leave money stranded.

B8.title: Says which outcome it is
B8.message: Every signed transaction carries a note naming the outcome it executes (agreed settlement, refund, ruling…), so the ledger history explains itself.

B9.title: No other outcome in progress
B9.message: Only one ending can be in flight at a time. If one was just signed and is still settling, a second one waits, so the deal can't be paid out twice.

B10.title: Right token issuer
B10.message: Every amount must be in the real RLUSD token from its official issuer, not a look-alike.

B11.title: The ledger would accept it right now
B11.message: Pre-signed endings can only be tried once: a failed attempt burns them. So the co-signer only signs one when the account is in exactly the state that makes it succeed, including being old enough to be deleted.

C1.title: Confirms the guest's actual booking
C1.message: The hotel's confirmation must point to the guest's own booking request.

C2.title: Right city and dates
C2.message: The confirmed city and check-in/check-out dates must match what the guest asked for.

C4.title: Right price
C4.message: The confirmed total must equal the room price the guest paid in.

C5.title: Deposit within the guest's limit
C5.message: The security deposit the hotel asks for must not exceed the maximum the guest agreed to. Otherwise the confirmation doesn't count.

K1.title: Guest checked in
K1.message: The hotel has recorded the guest's arrival, and the deposit is in the account.

K2.title: Deposit is exactly right
K2.message: The account holds the room price plus exactly the confirmed deposit, no more, no less.

S2.title: Valid settlement
S2.message: An agreed settlement splits the money between guest and hotel and closes the account, in one transaction.

S4.title: Correct service fee
S4.message: The service takes 0.5% of whatever the hotel receives. Refunds to the guest carry no fee.

S5.title: Guest left a review
S5.message: A stay that happened settles together with the guest's review, so every completed booking leaves a reputation record.

S6.title: Pays only guest, hotel and fee
S6.message: A settlement can only pay the guest, the hotel, and the service fee, never the arbiters or anyone else.

F1.title: Hotel admitted the problem
F1.message: There must be an open check-in dispute from the guest, and the hotel's own statement conceding it.

F2.title: Valid refund
F2.message: A conceded refund sends everything to the guest and closes the account, in one transaction.

F3.title: Full refund
F3.message: Everything in the account goes back to the guest, including any deposit and the dispute bond, with no fee.

R1.title: Refund is due
R1.message: The automatic refund is only for a booking the hotel never confirmed by its deadline. If the hotel confirmed in time, it doesn't apply.

R2.title: Account holds just the room price
R2.message: This refund was signed in advance for exactly the room price. If anything else is in the account now (a deposit, a dispute bond), it no longer fits.

R3.title: Valid refund
R3.message: The automatic refund sends the room price back to the guest and closes the account.

N1.title: No-show is due
N1.message: A no-show only counts after the last check-in time and after the guest's window to dispute at check-in has closed.

N2.title: Booking was confirmed
N2.message: Only a confirmed booking can end in a no-show. An unconfirmed one ends in a refund instead.

N3.title: Guest never checked in
N3.message: If the guest arrived and paid the deposit, it isn't a no-show.

N4.title: No open dispute
N4.message: If the guest filed a dispute (with its bond), the automatic endings wait for the arbiter. Silence can't override a raised flag.

N5.title: Account holds just the room price
N5.message: The no-show ending was signed in advance for exactly the room price. If anything else is in the account now, it no longer fits.

N6.title: Valid no-show payout
N6.message: The no-show ending pays the room to the hotel (less the fee) and closes the account.

N7.title: Correct service fee
N7.message: The service takes 0.5% of whatever the hotel receives.

L1.title: Release is due
L1.message: The 'nobody acted' release only fires after the guest's window to dispute has closed, and only for a stay that happened.

L2.title: No open dispute
L2.message: If the guest filed a dispute (with its bond), the release waits for the arbiter. Silence can't override a raised flag.

L3.title: Account holds room plus deposit
L3.message: The release was signed in advance for the room plus the deposit. If anything else is in the account, it no longer fits.

L4.title: Valid release
L4.message: The release pays the room to the hotel, returns the deposit to the guest, and closes the account.

L5.title: No deposit claim posted
L5.message: If the hotel claimed against the deposit, the release can't just return it: the claim has to be agreed, or ruled on.

L6.title: Deposit goes back in full
L6.message: The whole deposit returns to the guest; the hotel gets the room price less the fee.

U1.title: Primary arbiter's time ran out
U1.message: The backup arbiter may only rule once the primary arbiter's ruling window has passed without a ruling.

U2.title: Primary arbiter hasn't ruled
U2.message: If the primary arbiter already ruled, the backup steps aside.

U3.title: Backup arbiter has ruled
U3.message: There must be a signed ruling from the backup arbiter.

U4.title: Pays exactly what was ruled
U4.message: The transaction must pay exactly the amounts in the backup arbiter's ruling, to exactly those people.

U5.title: Valid ruling payout
U5.message: A ruling splits the money and closes the account, in one transaction.

U6.title: Correct service fee
U6.message: The service takes 0.5% of whatever the hotel receives.

D1.title: Hotel posted a claim
D1.message: A default ruling only exists to settle a deposit claim the guest never answered.

D2.title: Guest didn't dispute
D2.message: If the guest disputed the claim, the arbiter rules on the dispute instead.

D3.title: Guest's time to answer is over
D3.message: The guest can dispute a claim until the dispute window closes. Only after that does an unanswered claim stand.

D4.title: Claim within the deposit
D4.message: A claim can never exceed the security deposit.

D5.title: Pays exactly the claim
D5.message: The hotel gets the room plus the claim (less the fee); the rest of the deposit goes back to the guest.
